F-15.summary: backend/alembic/versions/002_seed_items.py:55-58 calls op.execute(sa.text(...), item) with a 2nd positional arg; alembic 1.13.1 Operations.execute signature is (self, sqltext, *, execution_options=None) -> raises TypeError: execute() takes 2 positional arguments but 3 were given. So 001->002 chain cannot reach head; item_bank seed (19 rows) is never applied via migration. Root cause was latent because there is NO repo-wide alembic execution path (zero hits in CI/compose/deploy/scripts/runbook/Dockerfile); real table creation uses Base.metadata.create_all (app/core/database.py:42, app/db/init_db.py:15, tests/conftest.py:68). Verified on isolated :55432 postgres 15.18: upgrade 001 exit 0 (8 tables + alembic_version), downgrade base exit 0 (clean), upgrade head exit 1 (TypeError at 002 line 55).
F-15.disposition: Recorded by M0-004 read-only audit; NOT fixed in M0-004 (002_seed_items.py is out of the audit's forbidden-to-change scope). Requires separate FIX-M0-004-001 before M2 Knowledge Core migrations rely on the alembic chain. Candidate fix: op.get_bind().execute(sa.text(...), item) or sa.text(...).bindparams(**item); also review 002 seed idempotency + wide DELETE downgrade per 50-database rules.
F-15.blocksMilestone: M2 (not M0/M1); on M0 critical path only as a recorded finding

F-16.summary: backend/alembic/env.py:26-29 wraps the whole online run_migrations() in a SINGLE context.begin_transaction() and does NOT set transaction_per_migration=True. Consequence: when 'upgrade head' fails at 002 (F-15 TypeError), the rollback spans the entire transaction, so the already-applied 001 DDL + alembic_version write are rolled back too -> DB ends at base (current=base), NOT at 001. Verified on isolated :55432 (Goal Orchestrator independent Max-Verify spot-check: alembic current exit 0, no revision line = base).
F-16.disposition: Recorded by M0-004 read-only audit (DB_API_BASELINE.md §1.6); NOT fixed (env.py out of audit scope). Severity P2 (Flash suggested P2; Max confirms P2: no product-runtime impact, but determines how the Release Gate 'migration up/down/up' evidence chain is read and how FIX-M0-004-001 acceptance is designed). Evaluate together with F-15 in FIX-M0-004-001: after fixing the 002 signature, decide whether to introduce transaction_per_migration=True so a failing step does not roll back prior committed steps.
